messages:
nina: heads-up — seeing a bunch of kafka produce failures today that trace back to header size limits. large chat requests + full span blobs in headers are pushing messages > 1MB and kafka broker rejects them. anyone else hit this?

michael: yikes. which headers are we stuffing? full OTLP protobuf spans in headers?

nina: yep. the gateway was attaching a serialized span bundle so workers could stitch exactly the same spans. worked for small payloads but not for long conversations.

tara: quick question — are these the binary proto blobs in a header named `x-rw-span-payload`? if so, kafka/java client treats headers as bytes; brokers still enforce max.message.bytes.

josef: i saw the same pattern in a customer bug. two options: (A) stop full rehydration and create a fresh child span at worker with `link` to trace id; (B) compress/encode the payload to keep header small. both have tradeoffs.

samir: on (A) you lose exact parent/child structure (can't preserve original span timings), but graph stays connected via links. simpler and future-proof. on (B) need cross-lang compression/encoding utilities and still hit opaque limits sometimes.

emily: thoughts on hybrid: always include minimal `traceparent` (W3C) + a tiny `x-rw-span-meta` JSON with sample decision + a short-hash pointer. full payload only for sampled/high-priority traces (flag in meta).

nina: hybrid seems promising. example header set we prototyped:

```
headers = {
  "traceparent": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01",
  "x-rw-span-meta": "s:1;h:0f4a3b;enc:zlib;v:1",
  "x-rw-span-blob": "<base64(zlib(proto))>"  # only when s=1 (sampled)
}
```

nina: consumer logic: if `x-rw-span-blob` present, decode and attach spans, else create new server span and add Link(trace_id=traceparent.traceid, attributes={"rw.sh":h}).

michael: two implementation asks: 1) a tiny cross-lang lib (go/java/python) for blob encode/decode and meta header generation, 2) broker-side metric to count header-size rejections.

josef: also watch out for baggage. baggage can blow up headers too. recommend capping baggage size and moving long values to a store with short token reference.

tara: vendor OTEL note: some instrumentation libs automatically serialize full span in propagation for "context carrier" patterns — we need to audit our custom propagators.

ops-bot: ALERT - kafka.produce.rejections spike on cluster-a (last 15m). triggered at 1976543205

emily: thanks @ops-bot — can we add an exporter-side scrub step that drops attribute-heavy spans when building header blobs? keep only a whitelist of low-cardinality attrs.

samir: agreed. also: sampling semantics — decide whether gateway sampling decision should be authoritative (i.e., gateway sets s=1) or worker may override. i prefer gateway authoritative to avoid rehydration surprises.

nina: decision proposal:
- default: propagate only `traceparent` + `x-rw-span-meta` (no blob). worker creates new span and links to trace id.
- sampled/high-priority: gateway sets `x-rw-span-meta` s=1 and includes `x-rw-span-blob` compressed proto.
- implement cross-lang encoding SDKs and header-size metrics.
- audit propagators to cap baggage.

michael: +1. please draft a short RFC with migration plan and breaking-change notes for Dedicated/private customers (they may have custom gateways).

josef: i'll start a spike for go/java libs. will post POC code snippet here when ready.

emily: i'll add the metric + alert tweak. also making a console card to surface header-rejection rate per client.

nina: ok team — thanks. action items: josef spike, michael RFC, emily metrics, tara propagator audit. i'll follow up with a PR for the gateway change. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: NOTE - thread pinned by nina

michael: small follow-up: we should document the exact header grammar in our API spec (examples, size limits, encoding). avoid ad-hoc header names across SDKs.

nina: agree. will include a migration checklist for partners.

samir: one more edge-case: delayed retries where a message sits in queue for hours — the worker should set a telemetry attribute `queue.delay.ms` when creating the new span. ensures SLO dashboards still show queue latency.

nina: good call. include that in RFC.

emily: closing loop: i'll wire a Grafana panel in infra dashboard to show header-rejections, avg header-size, and per-route sampling rate.

nina: thanks all, will sync in eng-platform weekly to finalize.
